reading.body:
Deb Fischer's recorded AI-related activity is one bill, S. 2296, plus two $2,500 PAC contributions from Meta and Amazon in 2025.

The fourteen events are not fourteen separate decisions. Eleven are votes on S. 2296 and its amendments, all cast between September 2 and October 9, 2025. She voted Yea on cloture, on the motion to proceed, on tabling an amendment, and on final passage. On the eight amendments recorded the same day, she split: two Yea, six Nay. The data does not name what any amendment would have done, so the split cannot be read as a position on any specific provision.

The two contributions are the only money in the record, both $2,500, from Meta's PAC in December 2025 and Amazon's PAC in February 2025. The page states no causal link between the money and the votes, and the dates do not establish one: the Amazon contribution precedes the September votes, the Meta contribution follows them. Two contributions from two companies is a thin basis for any pattern claim.

For AI specifically, this record shows legislative attention arriving as a single bill rather than a portfolio. It says nothing about data centers, power procurement, or interconnection, which is where compute constraints actually bind. A reader looking for a senator's role in the physical buildout of AI will not find it here. What the record does cover is narrow: one bill's procedural path and two committee filings.
